Name: Paracetamol
Primary Use: Treatment of fever and mild to moderate pain (headache, toothache, body ache).
Dosage Context: Adults: 500mg to 1000mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Do not exceed 4000mg (4g) in a 24-hour period.
Precautions: Avoid alcohol during use. Can cause severe liver damage if taken in excessive amounts. Do not combine with other products containing paracetamol.

Name: Ibuprofen
Primary Use: Relief of pain, inflammation, and fever associated with arthritis, menstrual cramps, or injuries.
Dosage Context: Adults: 200mg to 400mg every 4 to 6 hours with food. Do not exceed 1200mg daily for self-care unless prescribed.
Precautions: Take with food or milk to prevent stomach irritation. Avoid if you have a history of stomach ulcers, kidney disease, or cardiovascular problems.

Name: Aspirin
Primary Use: Pain relief, fever reduction, inflammation reduction, and low-dose cardiovascular protection.
Dosage Context: Pain/Fever: 325mg to 650mg every 4 hours. Cardiovascular protection (under doctor guidance): 75mg to 81mg once daily.
Precautions: Can cause stomach bleeding. Do not give to children or teenagers recovering from viral infections due to risk of Reye's Syndrome.

Name: Amoxicillin
Primary Use: Antibiotic for bacterial infections of the ears, throat, urinary tract, and skin.
Dosage Context: Adults: 250mg to 500mg three times daily or 500mg to 875mg twice daily, for a duration specified by a doctor.
Precautions: Take for the full prescribed duration even if symptoms disappear. Do not use for viral infections like colds or flu. Check for penicillin allergies.

Name: Omeprazole
Primary Use: Reduction of stomach acid to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and stomach ulcers.
Dosage Context: Adults: 20mg once daily in the morning, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast.
Precautions: Long-term use may reduce magnesium levels or increase risk of bone fractures. Avoid lying down immediately after meals.

Name: Cetirizine
Primary Use: Antihistamine for relief of allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itchy/watery eyes, and hives.
Dosage Context: Adults: 5mg to 10mg once daily, preferably in the evening.
Precautions: May cause mild drowsiness in some individuals. Avoid alcohol and driving or operating machinery if affected.

Name: Metformin
Primary Use: Oral diabetes medication to help control blood sugar levels in patients with type 2 diabetes.
Dosage Context: Adults: Usually starts at 500mg twice daily or 850mg once daily, taken with meals to minimize stomach upset.
Precautions: Monitor kidney and liver functions regularly. Avoid excessive alcohol consumption to prevent lactic acidosis.

Name: Atorvastatin
Primary Use: Cholesterol-lowering medication to reduce the risk of cardiovascular events like heart attacks or strokes.
Dosage Context: Adults: 10mg to 80mg once daily at any time of day, with or without food.
Precautions: Avoid grapefruit juice as it increases drug concentration. Report any unexplained muscle pain or weakness immediately.

Name: Albuterol
Primary Use: Bronchodilator for preventing and treating difficulty breathing, chest tightness, and coughing caused by asthma.
Dosage Context: Inhalation: 1 to 2 puffs every 4 to 6 hours as needed for bronchospasm.
Precautions: Can cause rapid heart rate, nervousness, or tremors. If your breathing symptoms worsen rapidly, seek emergency support.

Name: Lisinopril
Primary Use: ACE inhibitor used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and heart failure, and to improve survival after a heart attack.
Dosage Context: Adults: 10mg once daily, adjusted based on blood pressure response. Maximum dose is 40mg daily.
Precautions: Do not take if pregnant (causes birth defects). Can cause a dry cough. Seek emergency help if swelling of the face, throat, or tongue occurs.

Name: Loratadine
Primary Use: Non-drowsy antihistamine for managing hay fever, seasonal allergies, and skin rashes.
Dosage Context: Adults: 10mg once daily.
Precautions: Generally safe. Inform your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease before starting.

Name: Pantoprazole
Primary Use: Acid reducer used to treat erosive esophagitis, GERD, and conditions causing excess stomach acid.
Dosage Context: Adults: 40mg once daily in the morning, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast.
Precautions: Inform your doctor if symptoms do not improve after 2-4 weeks. Can interfere with vitamin B12 absorption over long-term use.

Name: Alprazolam
Primary Use: Benzodiazepine for short-term treatment of anxiety disorders, panic disorders, and anxiety caused by depression.
Dosage Context: Adults: 0.25mg to 0.5mg three times daily under strict medical supervision.
Precautions: Highly habit-forming. Causes drowsiness, dizziness, and coordination issues. Never mix with alcohol or other sedatives.

Name: Tramadol
Primary Use: Opioid analgesic for managing moderate to moderately severe pain.
Dosage Context: Adults: 50mg to 100mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Maximum dose is 400mg per day.
Precautions: Risk of addiction, abuse, and misuse. May cause severe drowsiness, dizziness, or respiratory depression. Avoid alcohol completely.

Name: Ondansetron
Primary Use: Prevention and treatment of nausea and vomiting, especially post-operative or chemotherapy-induced.
Dosage Context: Adults: 4mg to 8mg taken 30 minutes before symptoms or as directed by a doctor.
Precautions: May cause headache, constipation, or dizziness. Consult a doctor if you have a history of heart rhythm problems (QT prolongation).

Name: Montelukast
Primary Use: Maintenance treatment of asthma and relief of seasonal allergy symptoms.
Dosage Context: Adults: 10mg once daily in the evening.
Precautions: Not a rescue inhaler; do not use to treat sudden asthma attacks. Report any mood or behavior changes to your doctor immediately.

Name: Azithromycin
Primary Use: Macrolide antibiotic for treating respiratory, skin, ear, and sexually transmitted infections.
Dosage Context: Adults: 500mg on Day 1, followed by 250mg once daily on Days 2 to 5.
Precautions: Take as prescribed. Complete the full course. Common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, and abdominal pain.

Name: Ciprofloxacin
Primary Use: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat serious urinary tract, abdominal, bone, and skin bacterial infections.
Dosage Context: Adults: 250mg to 500mg twice daily for 3 to 14 days based on infection type.
Precautions: Avoid taking with dairy products or calcium-fortified juices. Increased risk of tendonitis or tendon rupture. Avoid sun exposure.

Name: Famotidine
Primary Use: H2 blocker to treat and prevent heartburn, acid indigestion, and gastrointestinal ulcers.
Dosage Context: Adults: 10mg to 20mg once or twice daily, taken 15 to 60 minutes before eating food or drinking drinks that cause heartburn.
Precautions: Limit intake of trigger foods (spicy, fatty, acidic foods). Consult doctor if heartburn symptoms persist for more than 2 weeks.

Name: Melatonin
Primary Use: Natural sleep aid for temporary relief of insomnia, jet lag, and regulating sleep cycles.
Dosage Context: Adults: 1mg to 5mg taken 30 to 60 minutes before bedtime.
Precautions: May cause daytime drowsiness. Do not drive or operate machinery within 4 to 5 hours of taking. Limit use to short periods.
